newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stands by 1997 economic goals - Aninat.
newsitem.headline: Chile stands by 1997 economic goals - Aninat.

text.p: Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat ratified the government's main targets for Chile's economy next year, saying it will post seven percent growth this year and 5.5 to six percent in 1997.
Aninat, in a speech to Congress in Valparaiso, said the government stood by its target of 6.5 percent inflation this year and 5.5 percent in 1997.
Although he gave no new major targets, his speech was significant in that it showed the government did not share private economists' views that growth will outstrip official forecasts.

"In 1997, we will work to continue our progress in these areas and to reach our inflation goal of 5.5 percent, coinciding with targets agreed with the Central Bank," he told legislators in his annual speech on the state of the economy.
His reaffirmation of the inflation and growth forecasts also suggested he saw no early relaxing of restrictive monetary policies by the Central Bank.
Both Aninat and Central Bank president Carlos Massad said last month they expected no lowering of interest rates until the first half of 1997.
